column5: fam_leading_zero_normalize docstring (tools/limine-pin-battery-r97.py:1819-1820) claims a text-compare gate orders "000000012.9.4" as era B; measured: "000000012.9.4">="12.9.5" is False and ("000000012","9","4")>=("12","9","5") is False, so it reads era A (correct). The family still discriminates a text-compare defect, but on 12.000000009.000000005 (int era B, text era A), not on the named member. Frozen claims C1 predicate itself does not repeat the false member (it states only "accepted with its era's own answer") so this is a docstring wording defect, not a claim falsification; supports any docstring-correction amendment. r96 spotcheck routed defect 2 is the same class (docstring era sentence false).

Z family is load-bearing for the axis claim: a gate otherwise conforming but reading Z=999999999 as era A fails exactly [REFUSAL-VERSIONS-9DIGIT-Z] 104/105, 0 error rows, 3 runs. But only 2/4 members discriminate (12.9.999999999); the two era-A members (0.9.999999999) are acceptance-only since era A answers prompt under both readings. Claim scope stands; the 4-member cycle is redundancy, not falsification.

LEADING-ZERO-NORMALIZE is load-bearing: a text-compare gate fails exactly [LEADING-ZERO-NORMALIZE] 104/105, 0 error rows, 3 runs. Only 1/4 members discriminate (12.000000009.000000005); the other three are acceptance-only under text compare (all read era A either way). N06 (refuse any leading zero) is the stronger discriminator: all four members refuse. No falsification of the frozen numbers.

N05 6 rows (4 Z + 2 LZ) and N06 4 rows (LZ) are exactly as frozen in both layouts (canonical + clone, 3 runs each, ExecBend receipts), all bad-output JSONDecodeError rc=64. N05's extra two LZ failures are the named 9-digit-Z members of LZ (params already state this in Limits); not a single-family bend and not claimed as one.

A3 already narrows the C1 do-nothing blindness sentence: leading-zero was sampled by the r96 instrument's --usage-check (reads unmet on N06), so the r96 blindness is roster-leg-only for LZ and full for Z. The frozen C1 target numbers (103/103) describe the roster leg and stand. Ledger records the amendment pointer; no number falsified.

All seven bindings are value comparisons (captured string vs derived string): argparse default, selftest total, schema literal, roster AST count x2, calibration selftest total, variant span. Each derive reads tool bytes (regex/AST/subprocess --selftest), none is a constant answer. RC-SCHEMA compares the full token (schema `...`), so a stale token with different digits still fails; not token-presence only.

Selftest-tally bindings read the printed tally only (parse_tally accepts any "selftest PASS N/N" line; a tool that prints a tally without running cases would satisfy the binding). This is the plan's named limit (d), already declared. Measured: a bare "selftest PASS 39/39" and "PASS (39 cases, 39 passed, 0 failed)" parse; trailing prose after the tally is rejected (fail-closed); 0/0 parses as (0,0) but is not N/N equal so it fails at the N/N check. No falsification; the limit is scoped.

Doctor-first capture does not hide a stale cell: a doctored token placed before the real one still fires RC-VALUE-MISMATCH because re.search takes the first (doctored) match and compares it. AST-count doctor (extra family name) fires both roster bindings. A second schema-like literal does not create a false pass (derive expects exactly one match).

Selftest is 12/12 and each case fires exactly its listed ids (independently recount: clean 0, six one-cell 1 each, row-missing 1, tool-missing 3 RC-DERIVE-FAILED for the three limine-pins bindings of the removed tool, derivation-lie 1, tally-lie 1). "Exactly its own id" is true at id-list level; tool-missing fires the id three times (one per binding), which is the declared exact list.

Coverage blindness (PASS 154/154 on the doctored table) holds only at the pre-round base f48d1642 (tools_total 154). At the freeze commit a57e88cd the same doctored table reads coverage FAIL (tools_total 157, the round's three new tools unrowed until settle). Amendment A1 already pins the fair base and the corrected fixture (rev 46fae1ba). Claim numbers stand under the pinned base; the recipe's frozen "master at freeze" wording would have falsified the blindness leg had it not been amended.

At my last run sha256sum -c .ufo/waves/round-97/before/instruments.sha256 reads 19 OK + 1 FAILED (build-doctored-fixture.sh, corrected per A1); the after-fixture pin file reads 20/20 OK. C1/C2 scoring instruments are byte-identical. This is the amendment's stated effect, already narrowed; no silent drift.
